functions.name: avifVersion
functions.description: Returns a const, null-terminated string describing the libavif version.

functions.name: avifCodecVersions
functions.description: Writes a human-readable summary of codec versions into the provided 256-byte buffer.
requirements: Caller must provide a writable buffer of at least 256 bytes.
Output is a null-terminated string.

functions.name: avifLibYUVVersion
functions.description: Returns the linked libyuv version as an unsigned int, or 0 if libavif was built without libyuv support.

functions.name: avifAlloc
functions.description: Allocates a block of memory of the requested size and returns its pointer, or NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: size is the number of bytes to allocate; may be 0 per C semantics (implementation-defined result).
Caller is responsible for freeing with avifFree().

functions.name: avifFree
functions.description: Frees memory previously allocated by avifAlloc().
requirements: Pointer p must have been returned by avifAlloc(), or be NULL (no-op).
Must not double-free the same allocation.

functions.name: avifResultToString
functions.description: Returns a static, human-readable string for the given avifResult code.
requirements: result must be a valid avifResult enumeration value.

functions.name: avifRWDataRealloc
functions.description: Reallocates the avifRWData buffer to newSize bytes. On out-of-memory, leaves 'raw' unchanged.
requirements: raw must be a non-NULL pointer to an avifRWData that has been zero-initialized before first use.
If returns AVIF_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY, 'raw' remains unchanged.

functions.name: avifRWDataSet
functions.signature: avifResult avifRWDataSet(avifRWData * raw, const uint8_t * data, size_t len)
functions.description: Sets 'raw' to a copy of 'data' of length 'len'. On out-of-memory, leaves 'raw' unchanged.
requirements: raw must be non-NULL and zero-initialized before first use.
data may be NULL only if len==0.

functions.name: avifRWDataFree
functions.description: Frees memory held by an avifRWData and resets its fields to empty.
requirements: raw must be non-NULL.
Safe to call on an already-empty avifRWData.

functions.name: avifGetExifTiffHeaderOffset
functions.signature: avifResult avifGetExifTiffHeaderOffset(const uint8_t * exif, size_t exifSize, size_t * offset)
functions.description: Validates the first bytes of an Exif payload and finds the TIFF header offset (up to UINT32_MAX).
requirements: exif points to Exif payload; may be NULL only if exifSize==0.
offset must be non-NULL and will be set on success.

functions.name: avifGetExifOrientationOffset
functions.signature: avifResult avifGetExifOrientationOffset(const uint8_t * exif, size_t exifSize, size_t * offset)
functions.description: Finds the offset to the Exif 8-bit orientation value. Returns OK on success or an error. If set to exifSize, no orientation tag was found.
requirements: exif points to Exif payload; may be NULL only if exifSize==0.
offset must be non-NULL; on success may be set to exifSize to indicate 'not found' without parse error.

functions.name: avifPixelFormatToString
functions.description: Returns a static string name for the given avifPixelFormat value.
requirements: format should be a valid avifPixelFormat enumeration value.

functions.name: avifGetPixelFormatInfo
functions.description: Fills avifPixelFormatInfo for the given pixel format per AV1 spec. For monochrome (YUV400), chroma shifts are set to 1 but should be ignored.
requirements: info must be a non-NULL pointer to writable storage.
format must be a valid avifPixelFormat.

functions.name: avifColorPrimariesGetValues
functions.description: Writes chromaticity coordinates (rX,rY,gX,gY,bX,bY,wX,wY) corresponding to the given color primaries code.
requirements: outPrimaries must point to an array of at least 8 floats.

functions.name: avifColorPrimariesFind
functions.signature: avifColorPrimaries avifColorPrimariesFind(const float inPrimaries[8], const char ** outName)
functions.description: Returns the closest matching avifColorPrimaries enum given 8 chromaticity values; optionally sets a human-readable name.
requirements: inPrimaries must point to an array of at least 8 floats.
outName may be NULL if the caller does not want the name.

functions.name: avifTransferCharacteristicsGetGamma
functions.description: If the transfer characteristics can be expressed as a simple gamma, stores that gamma and returns OK; otherwise returns an error.
requirements: gamma must be a non-NULL pointer to writable float.
atc must be a valid avifTransferCharacteristics value.

functions.name: avifTransferCharacteristicsFindByGamma
functions.description: Returns the transfer characteristics that corresponds to a simple gamma, if any.

functions.name: avifDiagnosticsClearError
functions.description: Clears the diagnostics error buffer in the given avifDiagnostics structure.
requirements: diag must be non-NULL.

functions.name: avifDoubleToSignedFraction
functions.description: Approximates the double v as an int32/uint32 signed fraction. Returns AVIF_FALSE if v is NaN or |v| > INT32_MAX.
requirements: fraction must be non-NULL.
v must be finite and within [-INT32_MAX, INT32_MAX] for success.

functions.name: avifDoubleToUnsignedFraction
functions.description: Approximates the double v as a uint32/uint32 unsigned fraction. Returns AVIF_FALSE if v < 0, v > UINT32_MAX, or v is NaN.
requirements: fraction must be non-NULL.
v must be finite and within [0, UINT32_MAX] for success.

functions.name: avifCropRectFromCleanApertureBox
functions.signature: avifBool avifCropRectFromCleanApertureBox(avifCropRect * cropRect, const avifCleanApertureBox * clap, uint32_t imageW, uint32_t imageH, avifDiagnostics * diag)
functions.description: Converts a Clean Aperture Box (clap) to an integer crop rectangle. Returns AVIF_FALSE if standards would be violated; outputs are then unreliable.
requirements: cropRect must be a non-NULL pointer to writable storage.
clap must be non-NULL and contain valid denominators (implied by standard; failure returns AVIF_FALSE).
imageW and imageH are the full aperture dimensions of the image.
diag may be NULL; if non-NULL may receive error details.

functions.name: avifCleanApertureBoxFromCropRect
functions.signature: avifBool avifCleanApertureBoxFromCropRect(avifCleanApertureBox * clap, const avifCropRect * cropRect, uint32_t imageW, uint32_t imageH, avifDiagnostics * diag)
functions.description: Computes a Clean Aperture Box from a crop rectangle and image dimensions. Returns AVIF_FALSE if standards would be violated.
requirements: clap must be a non-NULL pointer to writable storage.
cropRect must be non-NULL.
imageW and imageH are the full aperture dimensions of the image.
diag may be NULL; if non-NULL may receive error details.

functions.name: avifCropRectRequiresUpsampling
functions.signature: avifBool avifCropRectRequiresUpsampling(const avifCropRect * cropRect, avifPixelFormat yuvFormat)
functions.description: Returns AVIF_TRUE if the image must be upsampled to 4:4:4 before applying the crop rectangle per MIAF/AV1 rules.
requirements: cropRect must be non-NULL.
yuvFormat must be a valid avifPixelFormat.

functions.name: avifCropRectConvertCleanApertureBox
functions.signature: avifBool avifCropRectConvertCleanApertureBox(avifCropRect * , const avifCleanApertureBox * , uint32_t , uint32_t , avifPixelFormat , avifDiagnostics *)
functions.description: Deprecated alias of avifCropRectFromCleanApertureBox(). Converts a Clean Aperture Box to a crop rectangle.
requirements: Same requirements as avifCropRectFromCleanApertureBox().

functions.name: avifCleanApertureBoxConvertCropRect
functions.signature: avifBool avifCleanApertureBoxConvertCropRect(avifCleanApertureBox * , const avifCropRect * , uint32_t , uint32_t , avifPixelFormat , avifDiagnostics *)
functions.description: Deprecated alias of avifCleanApertureBoxFromCropRect(). Converts a crop rectangle to a Clean Aperture Box.
requirements: Same requirements as avifCleanApertureBoxFromCropRect().

functions.name: avifGainMapCreate
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new avifGainMap with default-initialized fields. Returns NULL on allocation failure. The 'image' field is NULL by default.

functions.name: avifGainMapDestroy
functions.description: Frees an avifGainMap and its owned 'image' (if non-NULL).
requirements: gainMap may be NULL (no-op).
Do not use the pointer after destruction.

functions.name: avifProgressiveStateToString
functions.description: Returns a static string describing the progressive decoding state.
requirements: progressiveState must be a valid avifProgressiveState value.

functions.name: avifImageCreate
functions.signature: avifImage * avifImageCreate(uint32_t width, uint32_t height, uint32_t depth, avifPixelFormat yuvFormat)
functions.description: Allocates a new avifImage configured with the given dimensions, bit depth, and YUV format. Returns NULL if arguments are invalid or on allocation failure.
requirements: width and height must be valid image dimensions (implicit library limits apply).
depth must be one of the supported depths; if depth > 8, planes are uint16_t internally.
yuvFormat must be a valid avifPixelFormat.

functions.name: avifImageCreateEmpty
functions.description: Allocates a new empty avifImage suitable as a decode target. Returns NULL on allocation failure.

functions.name: avifImageCopy
functions.signature: avifResult avifImageCopy(avifImage * dstImage, const avifImage * srcImage, avifPlanesFlags planes)
functions.description: Deep-copies an image (pixels and metadata) from srcImage into dstImage. Also copies gain map metadata and planes, if present.
requirements: dstImage and srcImage must be non-NULL.
planes selects which planes to copy (e.g., color, alpha).
dstImage must be an allocated avifImage; existing planes may be replaced.

functions.name: avifImageSetViewRect
functions.signature: avifResult avifImageSetViewRect(avifImage * dstImage, const avifImage * srcImage, const avifCropRect * rect)
functions.description: Makes dstImage a shallow view into a rectangular region of srcImage without copying pixel data. Ignores gainMap field.
requirements: dstImage and srcImage must be non-NULL.
rect must be non-NULL and within the bounds of srcImage.

functions.name: avifImageDestroy
functions.description: Frees an avifImage and all owned memory, including gainMap if present.
requirements: image may be NULL (no-op).
Do not use the pointer after destruction.

functions.name: avifImageSetProfileICC
functions.signature: avifResult avifImageSetProfileICC(avifImage * image, const uint8_t * icc, size_t iccSize)
functions.description: Sets the ICC profile data for the image.
requirements: image must be non-NULL.
icc may be NULL only if iccSize==0 to clear the profile.

functions.name: avifImageSetMetadataExif
functions.signature: avifResult avifImageSetMetadataExif(avifImage * image, const uint8_t * exif, size_t exifSize)
functions.description: Sets Exif metadata. Attempts to parse Exif orientation and, if found, sets transformFlags/irot/imir. Invalid Exif may cause avifEncoderWrite() to return AVIF_RESULT_INVALID_EXIF_PAYLOAD.
requirements: image must be non-NULL.
exif may be NULL only if exifSize==0 to clear.
Caller should handle potential encoder error on invalid Exif when writing.

functions.name: avifImageSetMetadataXMP
functions.signature: avifResult avifImageSetMetadataXMP(avifImage * image, const uint8_t * xmp, size_t xmpSize)
functions.description: Sets XMP metadata on the image.
requirements: image must be non-NULL.
xmp may be NULL only if xmpSize==0 to clear.

functions.name: avifImageAllocatePlanes
functions.description: Allocates the requested YUV/A planes for the image, ignoring any pre-existing planes.
requirements: image must be non-NULL and have width/height/depth/yuvFormat set.
May overwrite previous plane pointers; previous data will be freed.

functions.name: avifImageFreePlanes
functions.description: Frees the requested planes on the image. Ignores already-freed planes.
requirements: image must be non-NULL.

functions.name: avifImageStealPlanes
functions.signature: void avifImageStealPlanes(avifImage * dstImage, avifImage * srcImage, avifPlanesFlags planes)
functions.description: Moves the specified planes from srcImage to dstImage without copying. After the call, dstImage owns the planes.
requirements: dstImage and srcImage must be non-NULL.
Only specified planes are transferred; srcImage loses ownership of those planes.

functions.name: avifImageAddOpaqueProperty
functions.signature: avifResult avifImageAddOpaqueProperty(avifImage * image, const uint8_t boxtype[4], const uint8_t * data, size_t dataSize)
functions.description: Adds a non-essential ItemProperty (or ItemFullProperty if version/flags are included) to the image by box type. Advanced use; misuse can create invalid files.
requirements: image must be non-NULL.
boxtype must point to 4 bytes specifying the box type.
If adding a FullBox, the first 4 bytes of 'data' must be version (1 byte) and flags (3 bytes), and must be included in dataSize.
Properties are added after libavif descriptive properties and before transformative properties; order affects transform application.
An avifEncoder supports up to 127 unique properties.
Users should validate resulting file with avifParse() to ensure correctness.

functions.name: avifImageAddUUIDProperty
functions.signature: avifResult avifImageAddUUIDProperty(avifImage * image, const uint8_t uuid[16], const uint8_t * data, size_t dataSize)
functions.description: Adds an ItemProperty (or FullProperty if version/flags included) using the 'uuid' box mechanism as defined in ISO BMFF.
requirements: image must be non-NULL.
uuid must point to 16-byte UUID.
If adding a FullBox, include version/flags as the first 4 bytes of 'data' and count them in dataSize.

functions.name: avifImageScale
functions.signature: avifResult avifImageScale(avifImage * image, uint32_t dstWidth, uint32_t dstHeight, avifDiagnostics * diag)
functions.description: Scales the image’s YUV/A planes in-place to the given size.
requirements: image must be non-NULL and contain allocated planes to scale.
dstWidth and dstHeight must both be <= AVIF_DEFAULT_IMAGE_DIMENSION_LIMIT.
dstWidth * dstHeight should be <= AVIF_DEFAULT_IMAGE_SIZE_LIMIT.
diag may be NULL; if non-NULL may receive error details.

functions.name: avifRGBFormatChannelCount
functions.description: Returns the number of channels for the given RGB format.
requirements: format must be a valid avifRGBFormat.

functions.name: avifRGBFormatHasAlpha
functions.description: Returns AVIF_TRUE if the RGB format includes an alpha channel.
requirements: format must be a valid avifRGBFormat.

functions.name: avifRGBFormatIsGray
functions.description: Returns AVIF_TRUE if the RGB format is a grayscale format.
requirements: format must be a valid avifRGBFormat.

functions.name: avifRGBImageSetDefaults
functions.signature: void avifRGBImageSetDefaults(avifRGBImage * rgb, const avifImage * image)
functions.description: Initializes an avifRGBImage from an avifImage: copies width/height/depth, sets pixels=NULL, rowBytes=0, and other default fields.
requirements: rgb must be non-NULL and writable.
image must be non-NULL.

functions.name: avifRGBImagePixelSize
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes per pixel for the given avifRGBImage configuration.
requirements: rgb must be non-NULL and have valid format/depth configuration.

functions.name: avifRGBImageAllocatePixels
functions.description: Allocates a pixel buffer for the RGB image according to its width/height/format/depth and sets pixels/rowBytes.
requirements: rgb must be non-NULL and initialized (e.g., via avifRGBImageSetDefaults()).
Width, height, format, and depth must be set to valid values.
Caller must later free with avifRGBImageFreePixels() unless pixels are replaced by caller.

functions.name: avifRGBImageFreePixels
functions.description: Frees a pixel buffer previously allocated by avifRGBImageAllocatePixels() and clears pixels/rowBytes.
requirements: rgb must be non-NULL.
Safe to call if pixels is NULL.

functions.name: avifImageRGBToYUV
functions.signature: avifResult avifImageRGBToYUV(avifImage * image, const avifRGBImage * rgb)
functions.description: Converts RGB pixels into the image’s YUV (and optionally alpha) planes. Performs depth/range conversions as needed. Fails if dimensions mismatch.
requirements: image and rgb must be non-NULL.
rgb->width/height must match image->width/height.
image must be configured with desired YUV format/depth/range.
rgb must have pixels, rowBytes, and valid format/depth set.

functions.name: avifImageYUVToRGB
functions.signature: avifResult avifImageYUVToRGB(const avifImage * image, avifRGBImage * rgb)
functions.description: Converts the image’s YUV (and alpha) planes into the provided RGB buffer. Performs depth/range conversions as needed. Fails if dimensions mismatch.
requirements: image and rgb must be non-NULL.
rgb->width/height must match image->width/height.
rgb->pixels/rowBytes must describe a buffer large enough for the conversion, unless using avifRGBImageAllocatePixels().

functions.name: avifRGBImagePremultiplyAlpha
functions.description: Premultiplies color channels by alpha in-place for the given RGB buffer.
requirements: rgb must be non-NULL and have pixels allocated.
Format must include alpha; ignoreAlpha should be false for effect.

functions.name: avifRGBImageUnpremultiplyAlpha
functions.description: Un-premultiplies color channels by alpha in-place for the given RGB buffer.
requirements: rgb must be non-NULL and have pixels allocated.
Format must include alpha; ignoreAlpha should be false for effect.
Alpha values of 0 may cause undefined/unclamped results depending on implementation (not specified here).

import random
from typing import List

# Data type: arbitrary binary data
# Target stub: FUZZ_PARAM_STR supplies a byte string payload to avifRWDataSet.
# We generate a variety of valid, interesting binary buffers (<=4096 bytes).

MAX_SIZE = 4096

def _rand_bytes(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _repeat_pattern(pattern: bytes, total: int) -> bytes:
    if not pattern:
        return b""
    reps, rem = divmod(total, len(pattern))
    return pattern * reps + pattern[:rem]

def _bmff_ftyp_like(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Construct a minimal ISO BMFF FileTypeBox-like header (ftyp)
    brands = [b"avif", b"avis", b"mif1", b"iso5", b"heic", b"heix"]
    major = r.choice(brands)
    minor = r.randrange(0, 0xFFFFFFFF)
    compat = r.sample(brands, k=r.randrange(1, min(4, len(brands)) + 1))
    body = major + minor.to_bytes(4, "big") + b"".join(compat)
    size = 8 + len(body)
    return size.to_bytes(4, "big") + b"ftyp" + body

def _exif_like(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # EXIF marker-like with TIFF header
    endian = r.choice([b"II", b"MM"])  # little/big endian
    little = (endian == b"II")
    tiff = endian + (42).to_bytes(2, "little" if little else "big") + (8).to_bytes(4, "little" if little else "big")
    exif = b"Exif\x00\x00" + tiff
    pad = _rand_bytes(r, r.randrange(0, 64))
    return exif + pad

def _xmp_like(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    start = b"<?xpacket begin=\"\xef\xbb\xbf\" id=\"W5M0MpCehiHzreSzNTczkc9d\"?>\n<x:xmpmeta xmlns:x=\"adobe:ns:meta/\">\n"
    core = ("<rdf:RDF xmlns:rdf=\"http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#\">"
            "<rdf:Description xmlns:xmp=\"http://ns.adobe.com/xap/1.0/\" xmp:CreatorTool=\"gen\"/>"
            "</rdf:RDF>").encode("utf-8")
    end = b"\n</x:xmpmeta>\n<?xpacket end=\"w\"?>"
    ws = b" " * r.randrange(0, 16)
    return start + ws + core + ws + end

def _icc_like(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # ICC profile header is 128 bytes; make a small multiple
    length = 128 + r.randrange(0, 4) * 128
    length = min(length, MAX_SIZE)
    data = bytearray(length)
    size = len(data)
    data[0:4] = size.to_bytes(4, "big")
    data[4:8] = b"lcms"  # CMM
    data[8:12] = b"\x04\x30\x00\x00"  # version
    data[12:16] = r.choice([b"mntr", b"scnr", b"prtr"])  # device class
    data[16:20] = r.choice([b"RGB ", b"GRAY", b"CMYK"])  # color space
    data[20:24] = b"XYZ "  # PCS
    data[36:40] = b"acsp"  # magic
    for i in range(40, len(data)):
        data[i] = r.getrandbits(8)
    return bytes(data)

def _box_like(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    boxtype = r.choice([b"clli", b"pasp", b"clap", b"irot", b"imir", b"uuid"])  # known box types
    payload = _rand_bytes(r, r.randrange(0, 64))
    size = 8 + len(payload)
    return size.to_bytes(4, "big") + boxtype + payload

def _interesting_sizes(r: random.Random) -> List[int]:
    sizes = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256, 511, 512, 1023, 1024]
    sizes = [s for s in sizes if s <= MAX_SIZE]
    sizes += [r.randrange(1, min(1500, MAX_SIZE)), r.randrange(1500, MAX_SIZE + 1)]
    return sizes

def _catalog(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    cat: List[bytes] = []
    # Empty and small ASCII/UTF-8
    cat.append(b"")
    cat.append(b"hello")
    cat.append(("\u2603 snowman " + str(r.randrange(0, 100))).encode("utf-8"))
    # Repeated patterns
    cat.append(_repeat_pattern(b"\x00", 128))
    cat.append(_repeat_pattern(b"\xff", 128))
    cat.append(_repeat_pattern(b"ABCD", 257))
    # Asc/desc sequences
    cat.append(bytes(range(256)))
    cat.append(bytes(reversed(range(256))))
    # Random sizes
    for s in _interesting_sizes(r):
        if s == 0:
            continue
        cat.append(_rand_bytes(r, s))
    # BMFF/AVIF-like headers and metadata-like payloads
    cat.append(_bmff_ftyp_like(r))
    cat.append(_icc_like(r))
    cat.append(_exif_like(r))
    cat.append(_xmp_like(r))
    for _ in range(3):
        cat.append(_box_like(r))
    combo = _bmff_ftyp_like(r) + _box_like(r) + _exif_like(r)
    if len(combo) <= MAX_SIZE:
        cat.append(combo)
    # Trim sizes
    cat = [c[:MAX_SIZE] for c in cat]
    return cat

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    cat = _catalog(r)
    idx = r.randrange(len(cat))
    return cat[idx]

import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# EXIF/TIFF helpers targeting libavif Exif parsers:
# - Exif header: b"Exif\x00\x00"
# - TIFF header: endian marker ("II" or "MM"), magic 42, and 32-bit IFD0 offset.
# - IFD: 2-byte entry count, entries (12 bytes each), 4-byte next-IFD offset.
# - Tag 0x0112 (274) is Orientation, type SHORT (3), count 1, value fits in 2 bytes.
# - We also include minimal required structure so avifGetExifTiffHeaderOffset and
#   avifGetExifOrientationOffset can succeed on many seeds, but we randomize variants
#   to exercise multiple code paths (endianness, extra tags, padding, subIFDs, etc.).
# - Keep size <= 4096 bytes.

TIFF_TYPE_SIZES = {
    1: 1,  # BYTE
    2: 1,  # ASCII
    3: 2,  # SHORT
    4: 4,  # LONG
    5: 8,  # RATIONAL
    7: 1,  # UNDEFINED
    9: 4,  # SLONG
    10: 8, # SRATIONAL
}

TAG_ORIENTATION = 0x0112


def pack16(val: int, be: bool) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">H" if be else "<H", val & 0xFFFF)


def pack32(val: int, be: bool) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">I" if be else "<I", val & 0xFFFFFFFF)


def tiff_entry(tag: int, typ: int, count: int, value_or_offset: int, be: bool) -> bytes:
    return pack16(tag, be) + pack16(typ, be) + pack32(count, be) + pack32(value_or_offset, be)


def align_to(data: bytearray, align: int) -> None:
    pad = (-len(data)) % align
    if pad:
        data += b"\x00" * pad


def add_ifd(entries: List[Tuple[int, int, bytes]], be: bool, base_offset: int, out: bytearray) -> int:
    # Build an IFD at current end of out; return offset (relative to TIFF base)
    ifd_start = len(out)
    out += pack16(len(entries), be)
    # Reserve space for entries and next IFD offset
    entry_pos = len(out)
    out += b"\x00" * (12 * len(entries))
    next_offset_pos = len(out)
    out += pack32(0, be)

    # Now fill entries, appending any out-of-line values and backfilling offsets
    cursor = entry_pos
    for tag, typ, value_bytes in entries:
        unit_size = TIFF_TYPE_SIZES.get(typ, 1)
        count = max(1, len(value_bytes) // unit_size if unit_size else 1)
        # Ensure exact size
        total_size = unit_size * count
        vb = value_bytes[:total_size]
        if len(vb) < total_size:
            vb = vb + b"\x00" * (total_size - len(vb))
        if total_size <= 4:
            # Place in the value field, pad to 4 bytes according to endian
            if be:
                val_field = vb.ljust(4, b"\x00")
            else:
                val_field = vb.ljust(4, b"\x00")
            value_or_off = int.from_bytes(val_field, byteorder="big" if be else "little")
            entry = tiff_entry(tag, typ, count, value_or_off, be)
            out[cursor:cursor+12] = entry
        else:
            align_to(out, 2)
            data_offset = len(out)
            out += vb
            rel = data_offset - base_offset
            entry = tiff_entry(tag, typ, count, rel, be)
            out[cursor:cursor+12] = entry
        cursor += 12

    # next IFD = 0 (none) for simplicity; left as zero
    return ifd_start - base_offset


def build_minimal_exif(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    be = rnd.choice([True, False])

    # Start with Exif header
    data = bytearray(b"Exif\x00\x00")

    # TIFF header begins immediately after Exif header
    tiff_base = len(data)
    data += b"MM" if be else b"II"
    data += pack16(42, be)

    # We'll place IFD right after header (offset 8 from TIFF base)
    first_ifd_offset = 8
    data += pack32(first_ifd_offset, be)

    # Ensure we have space up to base+8
    while len(data) < tiff_base + first_ifd_offset:
        data += b"\x00"

    # Build IFD entries: orientation plus some optional extras
    entries: List[Tuple[int, int, bytes]] = []

    # Orientation tag (SHORT, count=1), valid values 1-8
    orientation_val = rnd.randint(1, 8)
    entries.append((TAG_ORIENTATION, 3, pack16(orientation_val, be)))

    # Optionally add XResolution and YResolution (RATIONAL)
    if rnd.random() < 0.7:
        num = rnd.randint(72, 600)
        den = 1
        xrat = pack32(num, be) + pack32(den, be)
        yrat = pack32(num, be) + pack32(den, be)
        entries.append((0x011A, 5, xrat))
        entries.append((0x011B, 5, yrat))

    # Optionally add ResolutionUnit (SHORT)
    if rnd.random() < 0.7:
        # 2 = inch, 3 = cm
        res_unit = rnd.choice([2, 3])
        entries.append((0x0128, 3, pack16(res_unit, be)))

    # Optionally add Software (ASCII), ensure NUL-terminated
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        s = rnd.choice([b"libavif-fuzz", b"cameraX", b"unit-test"]) + b"\x00"
        entries.append((0x0131, 2, s))

    # Optionally add ExifIFDPointer to an empty Exif IFD
    exif_ifd_offset_rel = 0
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        # Reserve spot; will append a tiny Exif IFD later
        # Placeholder; we'll backfill after adding main IFD to know offset
        pass  # We'll add after we place IFD0 to keep flow simpler

    # Append IFD0 now
    ifd0_rel = add_ifd(entries, be, tiff_base, data)

    # Maybe add a real Exif IFD and then patch IFD0 with ExifIFDPointer (0x8769)
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        # Build a simple Exif IFD with a dummy tag (ExifVersion 0x9000, UNDEFINED length 4)
        exif_entries = [(0x9000, 7, b"0231")]  # ASCII digits without NUL by spec
        exif_ifd_rel = add_ifd(exif_entries, be, tiff_base, data)
        # Now inject the pointer into IFD0 by increasing its entry count by one
        # Simpler: append a new IFD containing only the pointer by rebuilding is complex; instead,
        # add a tiny second IFD0-like block and link via next-IFD. This still exercises offset traversal.
        # To do this, set next-IFD of the first IFD to point to a new IFD containing no useful tags.
        # But avif parsers usually only need the TIFF base and orientation; the existence of a next IFD
        # is enough to exercise code paths.
        # Patch next-IFD offset in first IFD to a small empty IFD placed after current data.
        # Locate first IFD position to patch next-offset: tiff_base + ifd0_rel -> entryCount(2) + entries*12
        first_ifd_abs = tiff_base + ifd0_rel
        entry_count = int.from_bytes(bytes(data[first_ifd_abs:first_ifd_abs+2]), byteorder="big" if be else "little")
        next_offset_pos = first_ifd_abs + 2 + 12 * entry_count
        # Build an empty IFD with a single tag: ExifIFDPointer pointing to exif_ifd_rel
        temp_ifd_entries = [(0x8769, 4, pack32(exif_ifd_rel, be))]
        temp_ifd_rel = add_ifd(temp_ifd_entries, be, tiff_base, data)
        data[next_offset_pos:next_offset_pos+4] = pack32(temp_ifd_rel, be)

    # Keep total size bounded
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]

    return bytes(data)


def build_with_padding_and_junk(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed ^ 0xA5A5)
    base = bytearray(build_minimal_exif(seed))
    # Randomly add leading padding before TIFF (still valid: Exif header must be immediately followed by TIFF header).
    # To stay valid, we cannot insert between Exif header and TIFF header. Instead, append trailing junk to test size handling.
    junk_len = rnd.randint(0, 128)
    base += rnd.randbytes(junk_len) if hasattr(rnd, 'randbytes') else bytes(rnd.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(junk_len))
    # Optionally duplicate Exif header at end (benign junk)
    if rnd.random() < 0.2 and len(base) + 6 <= 4096:
        base += b"Exif\x00\x00"
    return bytes(base[:4096])


def build_tiny_valid_without_orientation(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed ^ 0x5C)
    be = rnd.choice([True, False])
    data = bytearray(b"Exif\x00\x00")
    tiff_base = len(data)
    data += b"MM" if be else b"II"
    data += pack16(42, be)
    data += pack32(8, be)
    while len(data) < tiff_base + 8:
        data += b"\x00"
    # IFD0 with zero entries
    data += pack16(0, be)
    data += pack32(0, be)
    return bytes(data)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    choice = rnd.random()
    if choice < 0.70:
        return build_minimal_exif(seed)
    elif choice < 0.90:
        return build_with_padding_and_junk(seed)
    else:
        return build_tiny_valid_without_orientation(seed)

import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generator for ICC profile data
# The fuzzer stub either clears ICC (size 0) or uses arbitrary bytes from FUZZ_PARAM_STR().
# We generate valid-looking ICC profiles of varying sizes and versions, plus a few edge/minimal variants.
# Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

# ICC profile header is 128 bytes. We craft a simple RGB display profile with minimal required tags
# (desc, wtpt, rXYZ, gXYZ, bXYZ, rTRC, gTRC, bTRC). Offsets are relative to start of profile.

MAX_SIZE = 4096


def _u32(v: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('>I', v & 0xFFFFFFFF)


def _s15f16(f: float) -> bytes:
    # Signed 15.16 fixed point, big-endian
    v = int(round(f * 65536.0))
    if v < -0x80000000:
        v = -0x80000000
    if v > 0x7FFFFFFF:
        v = 0x7FFFFFFF
    return struct.pack('>i', v)


def _date_tuple(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # iccDateTimeNumber: 6 x uint16 BE (year, month, day, hour, minute, second)
    y = rng.randint(1998, 2030)
    m = rng.randint(1, 12)
    d = rng.randint(1, 28)
    hh = rng.randint(0, 23)
    mm = rng.randint(0, 59)
    ss = rng.randint(0, 59)
    return struct.pack('>6H', y, m, d, hh, mm, ss)


def _pad4(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    pad = (-len(b)) & 3
    if pad:
        b += b'\x00' * pad
    return b


def _make_text_tag(text: str) -> bytes:
    # 'desc' type per ICC v4: actually there is a newer 'mluc', but many accept legacy 'desc'.
    # We'll build 'desc' type: signature 'desc' + reserved + ASCII count + string + null + Unicode/codepage fields
    # For simplicity, keep only ASCII part valid; set others to zero.
    ascii_bytes = text.encode('ascii', errors='ignore')
    data = b'desc' + b'\x00' * 4
    data += _u32(len(ascii_bytes))
    data += ascii_bytes + b'\x00'
    # Unicode language code/count and code page strings sizes set to 0
    data += _u32(0)  # uniCode length
    data += _u32(0)  # uniCode string (none)
    data += _u32(0)  # script code code page length
    data += _u32(0)  # code page string (none)
    return _pad4(data)


def _make_xyz_tag(x: float, y: float, z: float) -> bytes:
    data = b'XYZ ' + b'\x00' * 4
    data += _s15f16(x) + _s15f16(y) + _s15f16(z)
    return _pad4(data)


def _make_curv_tag_gamma(gamma: float) -> bytes:
    # curveType: signature 'curv' + reserved + count + values (uInt16)
    # For simple gamma, count=1 and value = gamma * 256 (approx per ICC, rough).
    # Many profiles use parametricCurveType ('para'), but curv(1) is common.
    val = max(1, min(65535, int(round(gamma * 256.0))))
    data = b'curv' + b'\x00' * 4 + _u32(1) + struct.pack('>H', val)
    return _pad4(data)


def _random_xyz_for_primaries(rng: random.Random) -> Tuple[Tuple[float, float, float], Tuple[float, float, float], Tuple[float, float, float]]:
    # sRGB-ish primaries whitepoint D65
    # XYZ for D65 white scaled Y=1: X≈0.95047, Y=1.0, Z≈1.08883
    # r,g,b TRC and matrix rows; for simplicity, use canonical Primaries XYZ coordinates of primaries
    # Standard rXYZ, gXYZ, bXYZ tags store the XYZ of the device primaries scaled so sum to white; we'll use common values.
    r = (0.4360747, 0.2225045, 0.0139322)
    g = (0.3850649, 0.7168786, 0.0971045)
    b = (0.1430804, 0.0606169, 0.7141733)
    # Add minor jitter to vary
    def jitter(t):
        j = 1e-3
        return tuple(max(0.0, v + rng.uniform(-j, j)) for v in t)
    return jitter(r), jitter(g), jitter(b)


def _make_tag_table(entries: List[Tuple[bytes, bytes]]) -> Tuple[bytes, List[Tuple[bytes, int, int]]]:
    # Build tag table (tagCount + records), but offsets/sizes unknown until we place data.
    count = len(entries)
    table = _u32(count)
    records_meta = []  # will fill later
    # Placeholder 12 bytes per record
    for sig, _ in entries:
        table += sig + b'\x00' * 8
    return table, []


def _build_icc_profile(rng: random.Random, target_size: int) -> bytes:
    # Prepare tag payloads
    desc_texts = [
        "sRGB IEC61966-2.1",
        "Display Profile",
        "Generic RGB",
        "Camera RGB",
    ]
    desc = _make_text_tag(rng.choice(desc_texts))

    # White point D65
    wtpt = _make_xyz_tag(0.95047, 1.0, 1.08883)

    rXYZ, gXYZ, bXYZ = _random_xyz_for_primaries(rng)
    rxyz = _make_xyz_tag(*rXYZ)
    gxyz = _make_xyz_tag(*gXYZ)
    bxyz = _make_xyz_tag(*bXYZ)

    # Gamma selection typical: 2.2, 2.4, 1.8
    gamma = rng.choice([2.2, 2.4, 1.8])
    rtrc = _make_curv_tag_gamma(gamma)
    gtrc = _make_curv_tag_gamma(gamma)
    btrc = _make_curv_tag_gamma(gamma)

    tags = [
        (b'desc', desc),
        (b'wtpt', wtpt),
        (b'rXYZ', rxyz),
        (b'gXYZ', gxyz),
        (b'bXYZ', bxyz),
        (b'rTRC', rtrc),
        (b'gTRC', gtrc),
        (b'bTRC', btrc),
    ]

    # Optionally add more tags to vary size but stay under limit
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # Add 'cprt' copyright as text tag
        cprt = _make_text_tag("libavif fuzz generator")
        tags.append((b'cprt', cprt))

    # Build header (128 bytes)
    header = bytearray(128)
    # profile size placeholder
    header[0:4] = _u32(0)
    # preferred CMM type (optional). Set to 'appl'
    header[4:8] = b'appl'
    # Profile version: choose v2.4 or v4.3
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        version = 0x02400000  # 2.4.0
    else:
        version = 0x04300000  # 4.3.0
    header[8:12] = _u32(version)
    # Profile/Device Class: 'mntr' (display)
    header[12:16] = b'mntr'
    # Color space: 'RGB '
    header[16:20] = b'RGB '
    # PCS: 'XYZ '
    header[20:24] = b'XYZ '
    # Date/time
    header[24:36] = _date_tuple(rng)
    # acsp signature
    header[36:40] = b'acsp'
    # Platform signature
    header[40:44] = rng.choice([b'APPL', b'MSFT', b'UNIX', b'\x00\x00\x00\x00'])
    # Flags
    header[44:48] = _u32(0)
    # Manufacturer, Model
    header[48:52] = b'\x00\x00\x00\x00'
    header[52:56] = b'\x00\x00\x00\x00'
    # Attributes (2 x u32)
    header[56:64] = _u32(0) + _u32(0)
    # Rendering intent: pick 0..3
    header[64:68] = _u32(rng.randint(0, 3))
    # Illuminant XYZ (D50 per spec) X=0.9642, Y=1.0, Z=0.8249
    header[68:80] = _s15f16(0.9642) + _s15f16(1.0) + _s15f16(0.8249)
    # Creator signature
    header[80:84] = b'lavf'
    # Profile ID (MD5 or zeros). Leave zeros
    # Reserved
    # header[84:128] already zero

    # Tag table
    tag_table = bytearray()
    tag_table += _u32(len(tags))
    # We'll compute offsets after placing data

    # Start building profile: header + tag table + tag records + tag data
    # Each tag record: signature(4) + offset(4) + size(4)
    record_size = 12
    records = []

    # Initial offset where tag data begins
    data_offset = 128 + 4 + len(tags) * record_size

    # Build records and data
    data_blob = bytearray()
    for sig, payload in tags:
        payload = _pad4(payload)
        records.append((sig, data_offset + len(data_blob), len(payload)))
        data_blob += payload

    # Constrain total size to target_size (<= MAX_SIZE). If too large, drop optional tags from end.
    def total_size_for(n_records: int) -> int:
        return 128 + 4 + n_records * record_size + sum(len(_pad4(tags[i][1])) for i in range(n_records))

    n = len(tags)
    while total_size_for(n) > target_size and n > 8:
        # Keep the core 8 tags; drop extras beyond n
        n -= 1
    # Rebuild with n tags
    tags = tags[:n]
    tag_table = bytearray()
    tag_table += _u32(len(tags))
    records = []
    data_blob = bytearray()
    for sig, payload in tags:
        payload = _pad4(payload)
        records.append((sig, data_offset + len(data_blob), len(payload)))
        data_blob += payload

    # Serialize records
    for sig, off, sz in records:
        tag_table += sig + _u32(off) + _u32(sz)

    profile_size = 128 + len(tag_table) + len(data_blob)
    header[0:4] = _u32(profile_size)

    return bytes(header) + bytes(tag_table) + bytes(data_blob)


def _make_minimal_blob(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Smallest plausible ICC-like blob with correct acsp header but empty tag table.
    header = bytearray(128)
    header[0:4] = _u32(128 + 4)  # header + empty tag table
    header[4:8] = b'appl'
    header[8:12] = _u32(0x04300000)
    header[12:16] = b'mntr'
    header[16:20] = b'RGB '
    header[20:24] = b'XYZ '
    header[24:36] = _date_tuple(rng)
    header[36:40] = b'acsp'
    header[40:44] = b'APPL'
    header[44:48] = _u32(0)
    header[56:64] = _u32(0) + _u32(0)
    header[64:68] = _u32(0)
    header[68:80] = _s15f16(0.9642) + _s15f16(1.0) + _s15f16(0.8249)
    header[80:84] = b'lavf'
    tag_table = _u32(0)
    return bytes(header) + tag_table


def _random_padding(rng: random.Random, size: int) -> bytes:
    return rng.randbytes(size) if hasattr(rng, 'randbytes') else bytes([rng.randrange(256) for _ in range(size)])


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose strategy for ICC payload generation
    choice = rng.random()

    if choice < 0.1:
        # Return empty payload (useful when stub chooses not to clear, still valid 0-size)
        return b''
    elif choice < 0.2:
        # Minimal valid ICC with empty tag table
        blob = _make_minimal_blob(rng)
        return blob[:MAX_SIZE]
    else:
        # Build a reasonably featured sRGB-like profile. Randomly vary target size within bounds.
        target = rng.randint(512, min(3072, MAX_SIZE))
        blob = _build_icc_profile(rng, target)
        # Occasionally append harmless padding to reach different sizes (some readers ignore trailing data)
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            pad_len = rng.randint(0, max(0, MAX_SIZE - len(blob)))
            blob += _random_padding(rng, pad_len)
        return blob[:MAX_SIZE]

        parts.append(f'    <exif:PixelXDimension>{w}</exif:PixelXDimension>\n')
        parts.append(f'    <exif:PixelYDimension>{h}</exif:PixelYDimension>\n')
    # xmpRights:Marked and WebStatement
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(f'    <xmpRights:Marked>{rng.choice(["True","False"])}</xmpRights:Marked>\n')
        parts.append(f'    <xmpRights:WebStatement>https://example.com/{_guid_from_seed(rng)}</xmpRights:WebStatement>\n')
    # dc:format
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        parts.append(f'    <dc:format>{rng.choice(FORMATS)}</dc:format>\n')
    # Custom extension namespace property (often appears)
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        parts.append(f'    <Iptc4xmpCore:CreatorContactInfo rdf:parseType="Resource">\n')
        parts.append(f'      <Iptc4xmpCore:CiEmailWork>author@example.com</Iptc4xmpCore:CiEmailWork>\n')
        parts.append(f'    </Iptc4xmpCore:CreatorContactInfo>\n')
    return ''.join(parts)


def _build_packet(rng, use_pi: bool, pretty: bool, include_misc: bool) -> str:
    # Root packet with namespaces
    attrs = ' '.join(f'xmlns:{k}="{v}"' for k,v in NS.items())
    start = ''
    end = ''
    if use_pi:
        start = XML_HEADER
        # Decide random xpacket end state (r/w)
        end_state = rng.choice(['w','r'])
        end = XML_TRAILER.replace('w', end_state, 1)
    indent = '\n' if pretty else ''

    # Optionally include x:xmpmeta wrapper (commonly present)
    wrapper_open = '<x:xmpmeta {attrs}>'.format(attrs=attrs)
    wrapper_close = '</x:xmpmeta>'
    if not include_misc and rng.random() < 0.5:
        # Simpler: put namespaces on rdf:RDF directly
        wrapper_open = ''
        wrapper_close = ''
        attrs_rdf = ' '.join(f'xmlns:{k}="{v}"' for k,v in NS.items())
        rdf_open = f'<rdf:RDF {attrs_rdf}>'
    else:
        rdf_open = '<rdf:RDF>'

    # One or multiple rdf:Description blocks
    descs = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 2 if include_misc else 3)):
        about = ''
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            about = f' rdf:about="uuid:{_guid_from_seed(rng)}"'
        desc = [f'  <rdf:Description{about}>\n']
        desc.append(_make_rdf_description(rng))
        desc.append('  </rdf:Description>\n')
        descs.append(''.join(desc))

    xml = []
    xml.append(start)
    if wrapper_open:
        xml.append(wrapper_open + indent)
    xml.append(rdf_open + indent)
    xml.extend(descs)
    xml.append('</rdf:RDF>' + indent)
    if wrapper_close:
        xml.append(wrapper_close + indent)
    xml.append(end)
    return ''.join(xml)


def _maybe_pad(rng, s: str) -> str:
    # Some producers add trailing spaces/newlines inside xpacket wrapper.
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        pad_len = rng.randint(0, 64)
        s += ' ' * pad_len + ('\n' if rng.random() < 0.5 else '')
    return s


def _clamp_size(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Ensure <= 4096 bytes
    if len(b) <= 4096:
        return b
    # Trim gracefully at a UTF-8 boundary (best-effort):
    trimmed = b[:4096]
    # Remove potential partial multi-byte tail
    while trimmed and (trimmed[-1] & 0xC0) == 0x80:
        trimmed = trimmed[:-1]
    return trimmed


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose profile
    profile = rng.choice([
        'empty',            # useful when harness decides not to clear (still valid minimal)
        'minimal_rdf',      # minimal RDF packet
        'with_pi',          # with xpacket processing instructions
        'rich',             # include multiple properties
        'lang_alt_heavy',   # emphasize language alternatives
        'array_heavy',      # many dc:subject entries
    ])

    if profile == 'empty':
        # A valid minimal XMP packet with minimal structure
        attrs = ' '.join(f'xmlns:{k}="{v}"' for k,v in NS.items())
        xml = (
            f'<x:xmpmeta {attrs}>'
            f'<rdf:RDF>'
            f'<rdf:Description>'
            f'</rdf:Description>'
            f'</rdf:RDF>'
            f'</x:xmpmeta>'
        )
    elif profile == 'minimal_rdf':
        xml = _build_packet(rng, use_pi=False, pretty=False, include_misc=False)
    elif profile == 'with_pi':
        xml = _build_packet(rng, use_pi=True, pretty=True, include_misc=True)
    elif profile == 'rich':
        xml = _build_packet(rng, use_pi=rng.random()<0.5, pretty=True, include_misc=True)
    elif profile == 'lang_alt_heavy':
        # Force many language alternatives
        rng2 = random.Random(seed ^ 0xABCDEF)
        def make_alt():
            return '      <rdf:Alt>\n' + ''.join(
                f'        <rdf:li xml:lang="{lang}">{_xml_escape(_rand_words(rng2))}</rdf:li>\n'
                for lang in LANGS
            ) + '      </rdf:Alt>\n'
        attrs = ' '.join(f'xmlns:{k}="{v}"' for k,v in NS.items())
        xml = (
            f'{XML_HEADER}'
            f'<x:xmpmeta {attrs}>\n'
            f'<rdf:RDF>\n'
            f'  <rdf:Description>\n'
            f'    <dc:title>\n{make_alt()}    </dc:title>\n'
            f'    <dc:description>\n{make_alt()}    </dc:description>\n'
            f'  </rdf:Description>\n'
            f'</rdf:RDF>\n'
            f'</x:xmpmeta>\n'
            f'{XML_TRAILER}'
        )
    else:  # array_heavy
        rng3 = random.Random(seed ^ 0x13579)
        attrs = ' '.join(f'xmlns:{k}="{v}"' for k,v in NS.items())
        items = [f'kw{n}_{_xml_escape(_rand_words(rng3,1,1))}' for n in range(rng3.randint(8,24))]
        bag = '      <rdf:Bag>\n' + ''.join(f'        <rdf:li>{i}</rdf:li>\n' for i in items) + '      </rdf:Bag>\n'
        xml = (
            f'<x:xmpmeta {attrs}>\n'
            f'<rdf:RDF>\n'
            f'  <rdf:Description>\n'
            f'    <dc:subject>\n{bag}    </dc:subject>\n'
            f'  </rdf:Description>\n'
            f'</rdf:RDF>\n'
            f'</x:xmpmeta>\n'
        )

    xml = _maybe_pad(rng, xml)
    data = xml.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')
    return _clamp_size(data)

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generator for ISO BMFF property payloads used by avifImageAddOpaqueProperty/UUIDProperty fuzzers.
# We produce a variety of valid-looking property box payloads, optionally with a FullBox header
# (1 byte version + 3 bytes flags) followed by box-specific data. Keep size <= 4096 bytes.

# Helpers to build small, self-consistent payloads for common HEIF/AVIF item properties.
# These are payloads ONLY (no size/type), as required by libavif APIs for properties.


def _u8(v: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('>B', v & 0xFF)


def _u16(v: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('>H', v & 0xFFFF)


def _u24(v: int) -> bytes:
    # 24-bit unsigned big endian
    return struct.pack('>I', v & 0xFFFFFF)[1:]


def _u32(v: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('>I', v & 0xFFFFFFFF)


def _i16(v: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('>h', max(-32768, min(32767, v)))


def _i32(v: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('>i', v)


# Property payload builders (no FullBox header)

def build_ispe(width: int, height: int) -> bytes:
    # ispe (ImageSpatialExtents): FullBox payload normally is: version(1), flags(3), width(4), height(4).
    # Here we return only the fields after the header; caller may prepend version/flags.
    return _u32(width) + _u32(height)


def build_pixi(planes: int, bits: List[int]) -> bytes:
    # pixi (PixelInformation): FullBox payload after header:
    # num_channels (1), then bits_per_channel (1 each)
    planes = max(1, min(4, planes))
    bits = (bits + [bits[-1] if bits else 8])[:planes] if bits else [8] * planes
    out = _u8(planes)
    for b in bits:
        out += _u8(max(1, min(16, b)))
    return out


def build_clap(width: int, height: int) -> bytes:
    # clap (CleanApertureBox) payload fields (unsigned, but interpreted signed for offsets):
    # widthN,widthD,heightN,heightD,horizOffN,horizOffD,vertOffN,vertOffD (all 32-bit)
    # Choose rational approximations within image bounds; denominators non-zero.
    widthN, widthD = width, 1
    heightN, heightD = height, 1
    # Center offsets (0)
    horizOffN, horizOffD = 0, 1
    vertOffN, vertOffD = 0, 1
    parts = [widthN, widthD, heightN, heightD, horizOffN, horizOffD, vertOffN, vertOffD]
    return b''.join(_u32(p) for p in parts)


def build_pasp(hspacing: int, vspacing: int) -> bytes:
    # pasp (PixelAspectRatioBox): hSpacing(4), vSpacing(4)
    return _u32(max(1, hspacing)) + _u32(max(1, vspacing))


def build_irot(angle_quadrants: int) -> bytes:
    # irot (ImageRotation): angle encoded in 2 bits in a byte (spec stores in lower 2 bits).
    return _u8(angle_quadrants & 0x3)


def build_imir(axis: int) -> bytes:
    # imir (ImageMirror): axis 0 (vertical) or 1 (horizontal) in lower bit
    return _u8(axis & 0x1)


def build_auxl(aux_type: str) -> bytes:
    # AuxiliaryTypeProperty: string with NUL terminator per HEIF
    s = aux_type.encode('ascii', errors='ignore')[:32]
    return s + b'\x00'


def build_colr_nclx(prim: int, transf: int, matrix: int, full_range: bool) -> bytes:
    # colr (nclx) struct: primaries(2), transfer(2), matrix(2), full_range_flag(1 with reserved bits)
    # Not a FullBox
    out = _u16(prim) + _u16(transf) + _u16(matrix)
    full = 0x80 if full_range else 0x00
    out += _u8(full)
    return out


def build_irot_full(angle_quadrants: int) -> bytes:
    # Some properties are FullBoxes; for those, we may include header ourselves.
    # But the fuzz stubs may prepend their own header. Provide header-less variant primarily.
    return build_irot(angle_quadrants)


def build_fullbox_prefix(version: int, flags: int) -> bytes:
    return _u8(version & 0xFF) + _u24(flags & 0xFFFFFF)


def build_uuid_payload(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # For UUID properties, payload is arbitrary. Provide small TLV-like data.
    tlv = []
    count = rng.randint(1, 4)
    for _ in range(count):
        t = rng.choice([0x01, 0x02, 0x03, 0x10])
        l = rng.randint(0, 32)
        v = rng.randbytes(l)
        tlv.append(_u8(t) + _u8(l) + v)
    return b''.join(tlv)


def _choose_valid_sets(rng: random.Random) -> Tuple[str, bytes, bool]:
    # Pick a known property and compose its payload. Also decide whether to include a FullBox header.
    # Many properties are FullBoxes (e.g., ispe, pixi, clap). Our fuzz stub may or may not prepend a header.
    # To ensure validity in both cases, we sometimes include the header ourselves, and sometimes not.
    width = rng.randint(1, 1024)
    height = rng.randint(1, 1024)
    depth = rng.choice([8, 10, 12])

    choices = []
    # name, builder, needs_fullbox
    choices.append(("ispe", lambda: build_ispe(width, height), True))
    choices.append(("pixi", lambda: build_pixi(1 if depth == 8 else 3, [depth] * (3 if depth != 8 else 1)), True))
    choices.append(("clap", lambda: build_clap(width, height), True))
    choices.append(("pasp", lambda: build_pasp(rng.randint(1, 65535), rng.randint(1, 65535)), False))
    choices.append(("irot", lambda: build_irot(rng.randint(0, 3)), False))
    choices.append(("imir", lambda: build_imir(rng.randint(0, 1)), False))
    # Common auxiliary type like alpha
    choices.append(("auxl", lambda: build_auxl(rng.choice(["urn:mpeg:hevc:2015:auxid:1", "urn:mpeg:mpegB:cicp:aux:alpha"])), False))
    # Color info nclx
    choices.append(("colr", lambda: build_colr_nclx(rng.choice([1, 6, 9, 11, 12, 22]),
                                                   rng.choice([1, 13, 16, 18]),
                                                   rng.choice([1, 6, 9, 14]),
                                                   rng.choice([True, False])), False))

    name, builder, needs_full = rng.choice(choices)
    payload = builder()

    # Randomly include a FullBox header if appropriate
    include_full = needs_full and rng.choice([True, False])
    if include_full:
        version = rng.choice([0, 1])
        # flags rarely used; keep small
        flags = rng.choice([0, 1, 0x100, 0x200])
        payload = build_fullbox_prefix(version, flags) + payload
    return name, payload, include_full


def _maybe_concatenate(rng: random.Random, first_payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Sometimes concatenate multiple property payloads to create richer data for UUID properties or opaque properties
    # Note: libavif treats the input as a single property's payload; concatenation is valid only for properties that
    # internally expect variable-length data. We restrict concatenation to UUID property style arbitrary data.

    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        extra = build_uuid_payload(rng)
        return first_payload + extra
    return first_payload


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Strategy:
    # - 60% generate a known property payload (possibly with FullBox header)
    # - 40% generate a UUID-like arbitrary payload (TLV) and sometimes prepend a FullBox header

    mode = rng.random()
    out = b""

    if mode < 0.6:
        name, payload, had_full = _choose_valid_sets(rng)
        # Optionally add a small extension to test parser len handling for that property
        if name in ("pixi", "auxl") and rng.random() < 0.3:
            payload += _u8(0)  # benign pad or terminator
        out = payload
    else:
        payload = build_uuid_payload(rng)
        # Optionally add a FullBox header to keep it looking like a FullProperty
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            payload = build_fullbox_prefix(rng.choice([0, 1]), rng.choice([0, 1, 2, 0x100])) + payload
        out = payload

    # Occasionally concatenate extra arbitrary section for more variety (kept valid for arbitrary types)
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        out = _maybe_concatenate(rng, out)

    # Ensure we respect size limit
    if len(out) > 4096:
        out = out[:4096]

    return out

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets fuzzer stubs that call FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to obtain C-strings
# used by:
# - avifCodecChoiceFromName(name)
# - avifEncoderSetCodecSpecificOption(encoder, key, value)
# It returns a single bytes buffer containing multiple NUL-terminated strings.

COMMON_CODEC_NAMES = [
    b"aom", b"dav1d", b"libgav1", b"gav1", b"rav1e", b"svt", b"svt-av1", b"avm",
    b"auto", b"AUTO", b"AvM", b"AOM", b"DAV1D"
]

LIKELY_OPTION_KEYS = [
    b"cpu-used", b"cpu_used", b"speed", b"tile-rows", b"tile-cols",
    b"row-mt", b"row_mt", b"deltaq-mode", b"enable-cdef", b"enable-restoration",
    b"aq-mode", b"tune", b"tune-content", b"enable-qm", b"qm-min", b"qm-max",
    b"max-quantizer", b"min-quantizer", b"cq-level", b"end-usage", b"profile",
    b"threads", b"passes", b"enable-intrabc", b"superres-mode", b"film-grain",
    b"enable-tpl", b"sb-size", b"lag-in-frames",
]

LIKELY_OPTION_VALUES = [
    b"0", b"1", b"2", b"3", b"4", b"5", b"6", b"7", b"8", b"9",
    b"good", b"best", b"realtime", b"aq", b"psnr", b"ssim", b"photo", b"film",
    b"on", b"off", b"true", b"false", b"auto",
]

ASCII_PRINTABLE = (string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " ").encode()

def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    L = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return bytes(r.choice(ASCII_PRINTABLE) for _ in range(L))

def _rand_utf8_like(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix ASCII with some multi-byte UTF-8 sequences and raw bytes
    L = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < L:
        t = r.random()
        if t < 0.7:
            out.append(r.choice(ASCII_PRINTABLE))
        elif t < 0.85:
            # 2-byte UTF-8
            c = r.randint(0x80, 0x7FF)
            out.extend(bytes([(0xC0 | (c >> 6)) & 0xDF, 0x80 | (c & 0x3F)]))
        elif t < 0.95:
            # 3-byte UTF-8
            c = r.randint(0x800, 0xFFFF)
            out.extend(bytes([0xE0 | (c >> 12), 0x80 | ((c >> 6) & 0x3F), 0x80 | (c & 0x3F)]))
        else:
            # Raw byte
            out.append(r.randrange(0, 256))
    return bytes(out[:L])

def _kv_pair(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    key = r.choice(LIKELY_OPTION_KEYS) if r.random() < 0.7 else _rand_ascii(r, 1, 16)
    if r.random() < 0.15:
        val = b""
    else:
        if r.random() < 0.6:
            val = r.choice(LIKELY_OPTION_VALUES)
        else:
            val = _rand_utf8_like(r, 1, 24)
    return key + b"=" + val

def _codec_name_variant(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        name = r.choice(COMMON_CODEC_NAMES)
    else:
        base = r.choice([b"aom", b"dav1d", b"libgav1", b"rav1e", b"svt", b"avm"]) if r.random() < 0.7 else _rand_ascii(r, 2, 10)
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            sep = r.choice([b"-", b"_", b" "]) if r.random() < 0.8 else b""
            suffix = r.choice([b"av1", b"codec", b"v1", b"fast", b"best", b""])
            name = base + sep + suffix
        else:
            name = base
        # Randomize case: operate on str then encode back to bytes
        try:
            s = name.decode('latin-1', errors='ignore')
        except Exception:
            s = ''.join(chr(b) for b in name)
        s2 = ''.join(ch.upper() if r.random() < 0.5 else ch.lower() for ch in s)
        name = s2.encode('latin-1', errors='ignore')
        if not name:
            name = b"auto"
    return name

def _join_cstrings(parts: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Join with NUL between entries and a trailing NUL to terminate last string.
    return b"\x00".join(parts) + b"\x00"

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Several codec names
    count_codecs = r.randint(3, 8)
    for _ in range(count_codecs):
        parts.append(_codec_name_variant(r))

    # 2) Realistic key=value pairs
    count_kv = r.randint(5, 16)
    for _ in range(count_kv):
        parts.append(_kv_pair(r))

    # 3) Standalone keys and values
    count_keys = r.randint(3, 8)
    for _ in range(count_keys):
        parts.append(r.choice(LIKELY_OPTION_KEYS) if r.random() < 0.7 else _rand_ascii(r, 1, 20))
    count_vals = r.randint(3, 8)
    for _ in range(count_vals):
        if r.random() < 0.6:
            parts.append(r.choice(LIKELY_OPTION_VALUES))
        else:
            v = _rand_utf8_like(r, 0, 24)
            v = v.replace(b"\x00", b" ")
            parts.append(v)

    # 4) Edge cases
    parts.append(b"")  # empty string
    parts.append(b"\x00")  # string that after split will yield empty prefix
    parts.append(b"aom\x00dav1d")  # embedded NULs inside one provided chunk
    parts.append(b"S\x00VT")

    # 5) Random blobs (sanitize NULs inside each part)
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6)):
        blob = _rand_utf8_like(r, 10, 40).replace(b"\x00", b" ")
        parts.append(blob)

    buf = _join_cstrings(parts)

    # Trim to <= 4096 bytes, keeping final NUL
    if len(buf) > 4096:
        buf = buf[:4095] + b"\x00"

    return buf

import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# This script generates small but valid AVIF/HEIF (ISO BMFF) files with
# a basic FileTypeBox (ftyp) and a minimal Meta box carrying a primary image
# item encoded as a trivial sample (no real AV1 bitstream). Although the AV1
# bitstream is dummy, the container structure is valid enough for libavif to
# parse, exercise IO paths, avifPeekCompatibleFileType, and sometimes proceed
# further depending on decoder leniency. We also vary brands and optional boxes
# to hit different code paths while staying within 4096 bytes.
#
# The buffers are suitable as inputs to FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME
# (when written to a temp file by the fuzzing framework).

# ISO BMFF helpers

def be32(v: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">I", v & 0xFFFFFFFF)


def be16(v: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">H", v & 0xFFFF)


def be8(v: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack("B", v & 0xFF)


def box(box_type: bytes, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    # size = 4(size) + 4(type) + payload
    return be32(8 + len(payload)) + box_type + payload


def full_box(box_type: bytes, version: int, flags: int, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    header = be8(version) + struct.pack(">I", flags)[1:]  # 1 byte + 3 bytes
    return box(box_type, header + payload)


# Box builders specific to AVIF/HEIF

def make_ftyp(random_state: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Compatible with avifPeekCompatibleFileType(): major brand must be 'avif' or 'avis'
    majors = [b"avif", b"avis", b"mif1", b"msf1"]
    # Ensure brand list contains avif/avis to pass the peek when desired
    ensure_brand = random_state.choice([b"avif", b"avis"])
    major = random_state.choice(majors)
    minor = random_state.randrange(0, 0x00020000)  # arbitrary minor
    # Build compatible brands list with some variety
    compat: List[bytes] = []
    pool = [b"avif", b"avis", b"mif1", b"msf1", b"heic", b"heix", b"heim", b"heis"]
    # Random number of compatible brands (1..6)
    for _ in range(random_state.randint(1, 6)):
        compat.append(random_state.choice(pool))
    if ensure_brand not in compat:
        compat.insert(0, ensure_brand)
    payload = major + be32(minor) + b"".join(compat)
    return box(b"ftyp", payload)


def make_free(random_state: random.Random, min_len=8, max_len=64) -> bytes:
    size = random_state.randint(min_len, max_len)
    payload = random_state.randbytes(size)
    return box(b"free", payload)


def make_meta_with_iloc_idat(random_state: random.Random, add_ispe: bool, add_pixi: bool) -> bytes:
    # We create a Meta box containing minimal properties and a single item whose
    # data is stored in a contained idat box referenced by iloc. This is a legal
    # HEIF structure variant supported by AVIF.
    # meta = FullBox('meta', version=0, flags=0) { hdlr, iinf, iprp, iloc, idat }

    # hdlr: handler type 'pict'
    hdlr_name = b"libavif-fuzz\x00"
    hdlr_payload = (
        be32(0) +  # pre_defined
        b"pict" +  # handler_type
        be32(0) + be32(0) + be32(0) +  # reserved[3]
        hdlr_name
    )
    hdlr = full_box(b"hdlr", 0, 0, hdlr_payload)

    # Build a tiny idat payload to act like an AV1 sample bitstream placeholder
    idat_payload = random_state.randbytes(random_state.randint(16, 64))
    idat = box(b"idat", idat_payload)

    # Item properties: ipco with ispe/pixi/colr as applicable, and ipma to associate to item 1
    ipco_children: List[bytes] = []
    associations: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []  # (item_id, property_index)

    prop_index = 1

    if add_ispe:
        # ispe: Image spatial extents
        width = random_state.randint(16, 320)
        height = random_state.randint(16, 320)
        ispe = full_box(b"ispe", 0, 0, be32(width) + be32(height))
        ipco_children.append(ispe)
        associations.append((1, prop_index))
        prop_index += 1

    if add_pixi:
        # pixi: pixel information (channels/depth). For AVIF, typically channels=3 or 4, depth=8/10/12
        channels = random_state.choice([1, 3, 4])
        depth = random_state.choice([8, 10, 12])
        pixi_payload = be8(channels) + b"".join(be8(depth) for _ in range(channels))
        pixi = full_box(b"pixi", 0, 0, pixi_payload)
        ipco_children.append(pixi)
        associations.append((1, prop_index))
        prop_index += 1

    # colr: set to nclx with sRGB-like primaries/transfer/matrix
    if random_state.random() < 0.7:
        prim = 1  # BT.709/sRGB
        tf = random_state.choice([13, 1])  # sRGB or BT.709
        mtx = random_state.choice([1, 6])  # BT.709 or BT.601
        full_range = 1
        colr_payload = be32(prim) + be32(tf) + be32(mtx) + be8(full_range)
        colr = full_box(b"colr", 0, 0, b"nclx" + colr_payload)
        ipco_children.append(colr)
        associations.append((1, prop_index))
        prop_index += 1

    ipco = box(b"ipco", b"".join(ipco_children)) if ipco_children else box(b"ipco", b"")

    # ipma: map properties to item 1
    # ipma version 0: entry_count, then for each item: item_ID(16), association_count(8), then associations
    # association: 1 bit essential (0), 7-bit index
    ipma_entries = []
    props_for_item = [p for (item, p) in associations if item == 1]
    assoc_bytes = be16(1)  # item_ID = 1
    assoc_bytes += be8(len(props_for_item))
    for idx in props_for_item:
        assoc_bytes += be8(idx & 0x7F)
    ipma_entries.append(assoc_bytes)
    ipma_payload = be32(len(ipma_entries)) + b"".join(ipma_entries)
    ipma = full_box(b"ipma", 0, 0, ipma_payload)

    iprp = box(b"iprp", ipco + ipma)

    # iinf: declare one item (infe) type av01
    # infe version 2: item_ID(16), item_protection_index(16), item_name (null-term), content_type (null-term), content_encoding (null-term), item_type(4)
    item_id = 1
    name = b"primary"
    content_type = b"image/avif" if random_state.random() < 0.7 else b"image/heif"
    infe_payload = (
        be16(item_id) + be16(0) + name + b"\x00" + content_type + b"\x00\x00" + b"av01"
    )
    infe = full_box(b"infe", 2, 0, infe_payload)
    iinf = full_box(b"iinf", 0, 0, be16(1) + infe)  # entry_count(16)

    # iloc: one extent pointing into idat payload
    # Use version 0, offsets/lengths 4 bytes
    offset_size = 4
    length_size = 4
    base_offset_size = 0
    reserved = 0
    sizes_byte = ((offset_size & 0xF) << 4) | (length_size & 0xF)
    base_byte = ((base_offset_size & 0xF) << 4) | (reserved & 0xF)
    loc_payload = be8(sizes_byte) + be8(base_byte) + be16(0)  # item_count follows
    # item
    item_construction_method = 0
    item_payload = (
        be16(item_id) +  # item_ID
        be16((0 << 4) | (item_construction_method & 0xF)) +  # reserved(12) + method(4)
        be16(0) +  # data_reference_index
        be16(1)    # extent_count
    )
    # Extent references idat content: offset is after the iloc box, but we can use construction method=0 with idat: offset is relative to idat payload start when method==1. We used method 0; for contained idat, spec uses method=1.
    # Switch to construction method 1 (from_idat) to be correct for contained data.
    item_payload = (
        be16(item_id) +
        be16((0 << 4) | 1) +  # method = 1 (from idat)
        be16(0) +
        be16(1)
    )
    # offset within idat
    extent_offset = 0
    extent_length = len(idat_payload)
    extent = be32(extent_offset) + be32(extent_length)
    loc_payload += be16(1) + item_payload + extent  # item_count=1
    iloc = full_box(b"iloc", 0, 0, loc_payload)

    # pitm: primary item id = 1
    pitm = full_box(b"pitm", 0, 0, be16(item_id))

    meta_children = hdlr + pitm + iinf + iprp + iloc + idat
    meta = full_box(b"meta", 0, 0, meta_children)
    return meta


def make_mdat_with_av1C(random_state: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Optional: provide an mdat that contains a trivial Annex B-like payload.
    # Not strictly necessary for parsing meta-based items, but increases variety.
    payload = random_state.randbytes(random_state.randint(32, 128))
    return box(b"mdat", payload)


def build_minimal_avif(random_state: random.Random) -> bytes:
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    parts.append(make_ftyp(random_state))

    # Optionally insert a free box to vary offsets
    if random_state.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(make_free(random_state))

    # Choose between meta/idat path or simple dummy mdat
    use_meta = True  # Favor meta since libavif commonly handles meta-driven items
    meta = make_meta_with_iloc_idat(
        random_state,
        add_ispe=random_state.random() < 0.9,
        add_pixi=random_state.random() < 0.8,
    )
    parts.append(meta)

    if random_state.random() < 0.4:
        parts.append(make_mdat_with_av1C(random_state))

    blob = b"".join(parts)
    # Constrain size
    return blob[:4096]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    # Randomly choose among several container variants
    variant = rnd.choice(["meta_idat", "meta_free", "just_ftyp", "meta_mdat"])  # but always include compatible ftyp

    if variant == "just_ftyp":
        # Valid ftyp with avif/avis brand only; useful for avifPeekCompatibleFileType
        return make_ftyp(rnd)

    if variant == "meta_free":
        data = make_ftyp(rnd) + make_free(rnd, 8, 48) + make_meta_with_iloc_idat(rnd, True, True)
        return data[:4096]

    if variant == "meta_mdat":
        data = build_minimal_avif(rnd)
        return data

    # Default: robust meta/idat build
    return build_minimal_avif(rnd)
